name: gap_fade_reversion_v116
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY gaps down >0.5% overnight, the first 5-10 minutes involve chaotic two-way flow as trapped overnight longs and opportunistic gap-extenders compete. Once NIFTY prints a 1-minute reversal candle — close in the upper 40% of its 1-minute high-low range and net positive over that minute — it signals that sell-at-open flows have been absorbed: VWAP-benchmarked institutional buyers, who are getting fills well below yesterday's close, have stepped in and overwhelmed the sellers. At 5-second resolution, we can detect this absorption signature (close-above-midrange + net 1-min gain) approximately 15-30 seconds before the bulk of the gap-fade impulse, entering with directional confirmation rather than blindly fading at open. This is structurally different from catching the first fade tick: we wait for the reversal candle to form, reducing false entries on gap-and-go days.

indicators.name: gap_pct
indicators.purpose: Overnight gap magnitude using first bar's open vs previous day's last close. No bar-period scaling — this is a day-level reference. Threshold 0.5% (~100 NIFTY pts) chosen to be larger than v103's 0.3%: v116 waits for confirmed reversal candle so the gap needs to be substantial enough that institutional VWAP absorption is unambiguous and not just micro noise.

indicators.name: net_return_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute (12 bars × 5s) net return. This is the 5-second analog of the original's 'close > open' reversal candle condition. On a 15-min bar the condition 'close > open' means the entire 15-min bar is bullish. Compressed to 1-min because we're targeting the first reversal confirmation, not the full candle. 12 bars gives exactly 60 seconds — long enough for a real reversal structure to emerge at 5s, short enough that we're still early in the fade impulse.

indicators.name: range_position_12
indicators.purpose: Close position within the 1-minute high-low range (0=at low, 1=at high). Threshold 0.6 for bullish (gap-down fade) and 0.4 for bearish (gap-up fade). This is the key differentiator from v103: the original's 'close > open' is structurally equivalent to price closing in the upper portion of the day's range, which at 5s maps to close above the midpoint of the 1-min range. A range position >0.6 means buying pressure dominated the last 60 seconds, confirming absorption.

conditions: net_return_12 > reversal_threshold (close above 1-min-ago close — reversal candle forming)
range_position_12 > 0.6 (close in upper 40% of 1-min range — bullish absorption)
time_minutes in [560, 585) — 09:20-09:45 IST (after initial volatility, before gap resolves)
buy_ce.confirmation: 1-minute reversal candle absorption structure (net positive + upper range close)

conditions: range_position_12 < 0.4 (close in lower 40% of 1-min range — distribution)
buy_pe.confirmation: 1-minute reversal candle distribution structure (net negative + lower range close)

exit.stop_rationale: 5 option points (~10 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5). After a confirmed 1-minute reversal candle, if NIFTY reverses another 10 spot pts against us, the absorption thesis has definitively failed — the gap is extending not fading. Slightly wider than v103's 4 pts because we enter ~5-10 min into the session when volatility is lower but moves can be more sustained; a 10-pt adverse move at this stage is unambiguous gap-and-go.
exit.target_rationale: 8 option points (~16 NIFTY spot pts). The post-absorption fade impulse on NIFTY — after the reversal candle confirms — typically covers 15-25 spot pts in the next 60-90 seconds. Targeting 16 pts captures ~65% of the median expected move (1:1.6 R:R). Wider than v103's 7 pts because we enter with higher conviction (confirmed reversal candle) and can afford a bigger target.

filters.vix_filter: vix 10-25 — same rationale as v103; below 10 means no overnight fear so gap is microstructural noise; above 25 means macro panic and gap won't fade behaviorally
filters.time_filter: 09:20-09:45 IST only — starts 5 min later than v103 (skip initial noisy open), ends 10 min later (allows time for reversal candle to form); gap fades resolved or structural by 09:45
filters.volume_filter: none — reversal candle structure (range position + net return) already implies volume; adding explicit volume threshold would over-filter at 5s resolution
filters.trend_filter: none — gap fade is mean-reverting; gap direction determines trade direction, not prior trend
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium-low — VWAP benchmarking and institutional gap-fade behavior is structurally persistent; reversal candle filter reduces crowding risk vs pure gap-fade

adaptation_notes: Original v116 trades top-50 F&O stocks on 15-min bars, holding 10-30 bars (2.5-7.5 hrs) targeting full gap fill to prev_close. Key conversion insight: the original's entry condition 'close > open' on a gap-down day is a reversal candle — the 15-min bar itself turned bullish. At 5s, this maps to the 1-minute close being in the upper portion of the 1-minute range AND positive vs 1-min-ago. Changes from original: (1) Target compressed from full gap fill (~200 pts) to post-absorption impulse (~16 pts = 8 option pts). (2) Time window 09:20-09:45 — 5 min later than v103 to allow the reversal candle to form, not just the first fade tick. (3) Replaced volume > SMA(volume,5) with range_position_12 — at 5s on NIFTY index, range position is a cleaner proxy for absorption than raw volume comparisons. (4) Differentiation from v103: v103 catches the FIRST fade impulse using 3-bar momentum direction; v116 catches the CONFIRMED REVERSAL using 1-min candle structure, trading fewer but higher-conviction setups.
weaknesses: Gap-and-go days (gap-down then continued down) will hit stops — 1-min reversal candle reduces but doesn't eliminate false entries
Fewer opportunities than v103 (only after confirmed reversal forms) — some days the reversal candle forms after 09:45 and misses the window
NIFTY index gaps of >0.5% occur on fewer than 30% of trading days, limiting frequency
First 5 min of session (09:15-09:20) excluded; may miss the fastest fade on strong gap days
